headline: Conclusions in omics and neural data shift with null models, evaluation depth and replicate noise
label: Evaluation Choice Robustness Audits
summary: Preprints show that null construction, evaluation depth and replicate structure can alter apparent effects and method rankings, motivating explicit robustness audits.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that reported effects and method rankings depend on analytic and evaluation choices, and several preprints quantify this explicitly. Rich-club analysis of Alzheimer's EEG can create or erase group differences depending on null network construction and hub re-identification. Proteomic co-abundance method rankings change with evaluation depth, with no method dominating. In drug-tolerant PC9 cells, replicate libraries set the noise floor, assessed by a library-level permutation test. The stroke efferocytosis study scores readouts against expression-matched nulls, and the striatal optogenetics reanalysis adds permutation and leave-one-out checks. spicyR v2 offers a permutation-free co-localisation test that corrects image differences. A conditioned sequence model predicts interferon-beta response but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects. Not all items are framed as audits.
